a.xlink:title: An all-reduce performed as reduce-scatter then all-gather around a ring, bandwidth-optimal for large messages but with latency linear in participants.
Coordinated data exchange and reduction across a process group.
All-reduce schedules over trees or hierarchical groups, with latency logarithmic in participants, suited to small messages and multi-level networks.
A cost model estimating message time as a fixed latency term plus message size times a per-byte cost, used to compare collective algorithms.
Performing collective reductions inside network switches so data crosses each link fewer times, lowering all-reduce traffic and latency.
An architecture in which workers pull and push model parameters from sharded server processes, common for sparse recommendation models and asynchronous training.

Choosing, per call, among collective algorithms (ring, tree, switch-offloaded) and wire protocols by message size, participant count, and link hierarchy, to minimize latency for small messages and maximize bandwidth for large ones.

A collective in which every participant ends with the same reduction, usually the sum, of all participants' equal-shaped tensors, the operation that synchronizes gradients across replicas in data-parallel training.

The complementary collectives in which each participant receives one reduced shard of the group's tensors (reduce-scatter) or the concatenation of every participant's shard (all-gather), the pair that moves sharded parameters and gradients in fully sharded training and composes into a bandwidth-optimal all-reduce.

A fabric in which accelerator nodes form a multidimensional grid with wraparound links to fixed neighbors rather than tiers of switches, so neighbor and ring traffic can run at link rate while global exchanges are routed hop by hop with lower bisection bandwidth that depends on dimensions, routing, and contention.
